counterexample: Let V={x,y} and T1=T2={{x,y}}. Then the constructed edge f equals e and therefore belongs to T1, contrary to step 0014.
assessment_summary:
0001: Merely the solution heading; no mathematical claim.
0002: Correctly fixes an arbitrary edge e={x,y} of T1 and invokes the bridge property of tree edges.
0003: Correct: deleting an edge of a tree produces exactly two tree components, named A and B.
0004: Correctly labels their vertex sets so that x∈VA and y∈VB.
0005: Correct: VA,VB partition V and e was the only T1-edge crossing this cut.
0006: Correct: a tree T2 has a unique path between x and y.
0007: Introduces notation for that path; justified by step 0006.
0008: Correctly writes the path from x=v0 to y=vk.
0009: Correctly states that consecutive path vertices determine edges of T2.
0010: Correct: a path beginning in VA and ending in VB must first enter VB.
0011: Correct: immediately before its first VB vertex, the path is in VA because VA,VB partition V.
0012: Correctly defines f as the corresponding crossing edge.
0013: Correct: f lies on the chosen T2-path and has endpoints on opposite sides of the cut.
0014: Incorrect: f need not be absent from T1; it may equal e when e∈T2.
0015: Incorrect as a continuation: membership f∈T1 does not imply a crossing edge other than e unless f≠e is first proved.
0016: The asserted contradiction is therefore unjustified, although this false claim is unnecessary for the exchange argument.
0017: Correctly announces the construction of the exchanged edge sets.
0018: Notational fragment introducing E′1; no independent claim.
0019: Correct definition E′1=(T1\{e})∪{f}.
0020: Notational fragment introducing E′2; no independent claim.
0021: Correct definition E′2=(T2\{f})∪{e}.
0022: Notational fragment introducing T′1; no independent claim.
0023: Correctly begins defining T′1=(V,E′1).
0024: Completes the preceding notation and introduces T′2; justified.
0025: Correctly begins defining T′2=(V,E′2).
0026: Completes the graph definitions and states the claim to be proved.
0027: Continuation of the claim that T′1 and T′2 are trees; appropriate.
0028: Completes that claim; no new inference.
0029: Section heading for the proof concerning T′1.
0030: Restates the subclaim that T′1 is a tree.
0031: Begins the edge-count claim for E′1; justified upon completion.
0032: Correct: T1 has |V|−1 edges and f∉T1\{e}, even if f=e, so replacement preserves the count.
0033: Correctly identifies connectedness and acyclicity as sufficient properties to check.
0034: Correctly recalls that T1\{e} consists of the disjoint trees A and B.
0035: Correctly identifies f as the newly included edge joining the two components (or restoring e if f=e).
0036: Continuation of the endpoint statement; justified.
0037: Correct: f has one endpoint in each of A and B and therefore reconnects them.
0038: Correctly concludes that T′1 is connected on all vertices.
0039: Introduces the acyclicity argument; no unsupported inference.
0040: Correct: T1\{e} has no path between VA and VB.
0041: Correct: adding an edge whose endpoints were in different components cannot create a cycle.
0042: Correctly describes f as the sole intercomponent connection in T′1.
0043: Concludes the acyclicity argument and begins the summary; justified.
0044: Correctly summarizes connectedness and continues the edge-count statement.
0045: Correctly states that T′1 has |V|−1 edges and no cycles.
0046: Correctly concludes that T′1 is a spanning tree.
0047: Section heading for the proof concerning T′2.
0048: Restates the subclaim and appropriately invokes the analogous exchange argument.
0049: Begins the edge-count claim for E′2; justified upon completion.
0050: Correct: T2 has |V|−1 edges and e∉T2\{f}, so the replacement preserves the count.
0051: Correct: deleting any tree edge f produces two components, and f lay on the unique x–y path.
0052: Correct: deleting an edge on the unique x–y path separates x and y.
0053: Correctly notes that e={x,y} is added to E′2.
0054: Correct: e reconnects the two components containing x and y.
0055: Correctly continues the conclusion that T′2 is connected.
0056: Correct: T′2 covers V, and adding e between distinct components creates no cycle.
0057: Correctly argues that an x–y path in T2\{f} would yield a second x–y path in T2.
0058: Correctly invokes uniqueness of paths in a tree and concludes the no-cycle argument.
0059: Correctly summarizes that T′2 is connected and acyclic.
0060: Correctly concludes that T′2 is a tree; the edge count is consistent though redundant.
0061: Correctly summarizes the constructed f and the exchange result for the arbitrary e.
0062: Notational continuation referring to T′1; no new claim.
0063: Notational continuation referring to T′2; no new claim.
0064: Correctly applies arbitrariness of e to obtain the universal-existential conclusion.
0065: Correctly restates the two exchanged graphs established to be trees.
0066: Stray page marker; no mathematical claim.
